claim_type: universally quantified over an infinite domain; finite experiments are scoped corroboration only

exact_statement.conclusion: E_{t ~ Unif[T]} ||grad F(xbar_t)||_c <= eps, with ||grad F(x)||_c = inf over couplings P with E[y]=x of ||E grad F(y)|| + c E||y-x||^2
exact_statement.quantifiers: for all eps > 0; c > 0; d >= 1; objectives F satisfying Assumptions 1-4; beta_2 in the theorem's stated band; T at least the theorem's stated complexity

informal_statement: Running Algorithm 2 (Exponentiated O2NC) with Theorem 5 (clipped Adam, Eq. 8) for the theorem's own T yields E[||grad F(x)||_c] <= eps, where ||.||_c is the (c,eps)-stationarity measure. the novelty is the RELAXED condition beta_2 in [beta_1^4, beta_1^2), a band that prior beta_2 >= beta_1^2 analyses forbid.
non_circularity: No formula-derived quantity is used as the primary evidence for the formula it comes from. Where a finite experiment cannot establish a universally quantified statement, the verdict is BLOCKED rather than VERIFIED.

paper.title: Dynamic Regret via Discounted-to-Dynamic Reduction with Applications to Curved Losses and Adam Optimizer

verdict_rule: VERIFIED requires no failures at the theorem's own T AND every negative control to fail as intended. A control that does not fire means the test has no power and forces BLOCKED.

verification_design.acceptance: mean + 2 standard errors over independent runs must be <= eps (conservative)
verification_design.algorithm: Algorithm 2 exactly: Exp(1) step scaling s_t, the EMA output xbar_t = (beta-beta^t)/(1-beta^t) xbar_{t-1} + (1-beta)/(1-beta^t) x_t, and the stated Adam update
verification_design.assumption_audit: Assumptions 1 and 4 are re-checked NUMERICALLY per objective rather than assumed from construction. This caught a real error: asym_valley's Lipschitz constant had been eyeballed and failed its own audit until G_F was computed from ||Q||_op, sqrt(d) and the numerically maximised |h(z)|.
verification_design.measure: ||grad F||_c is an INFIMUM over couplings, so it is upper-bounded by Gaussian smoothing; by Jensen this is conservative, i.e. the test can only be harder than the theorem requires, never easier
verification_design.non_vacuity_gate: eps = 0.6 * ||grad F(x_0)||_c, and every setting must START above eps. Without this the test is vacuous: an earlier draft started at approximately stationary points and 'passed' at T = 2 as easily as at the theorem's T.
verification_design.parallelism_note: runs are vectorised over the run axis for speed; this is validated against the scalar path (|z| <= 0.93 across objectives and both variants) and preserves per-run objective draws and start points

what_would_falsify_it: an objective satisfying Assumptions 1-4, with parameters from the theorem's own formulas and T at least the theorem's T, for which the expectation exceeds eps
